contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned systems thinking and sustainability. This week: your own capstone engineering-design project!

The engineering design process (introduced briefly last week) always starts with clearly defining a real problem, including who is affected and what constraints (limited budget, materials, or space) shape possible solutions. A vague problem like 'help the environment' is too broad; a defined problem like 'reduce food waste in my school's cafeteria, working within a zero-additional-cost constraint' is specific and workable. Choose a real environmental or sustainability problem you care about, and write a clearly defined problem statement including at least one real constraint.
You just defined a real engineering problem! Tomorrow we'll brainstorm and evaluate possible solutions.

objectives: Understand a well-defined engineering problem as specific, with real constraints
Write a specific, constrained problem statement for the child's own capstone project
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's engineering-design-process introduction briefly.
2. Introduce well-defined vs. vague problems using the food-waste example.
3. Have the child write their own problem statement with a real constraint.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's brainstorming lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer 2-3 familiar starting problems (school food waste, classroom energy use, water use at home) to choose from rather than an entirely open search
Ready for more: ask the child why including a real constraint (budget, materials, time) from the very start makes later solutions more realistic and useful
Opens this week's capstone-engineering-project thread from the course's own description, directly building on last week's brief introduction to the process
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended activity — check that the problem statement is specific (not vague), names who is affected, and includes at least one genuine, realistic constraint the solution will need to work within.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 9-12 Engineering Design standard HS-ETS1-1: analyzing a major global challenge to specify criteria and constraints, opening this week's capstone thread from the course's own description.
